item_title: New building codes ease height restrictions on hospitals
input_text:
New building codes ease height restrictions on hospitals

In a move aimed at curing the chronic shortage of hospital beds in dense urban centers, the government has notified the National Building Construction Standards (NBCS) 2026.    The new code removes long-standing height restrictions on healthcare facilities, finally allowing Intensive Care Units (ICUs) to be located above 45 meters.    For years, Indian hospitals were tethered to the ground by the building code, which restricted hospital heights to 45 metres or roughly 12–15 floors and mandated that ICUs remain below 30 metres.

signals.key_claim: NBCS 2026 removes height restrictions for healthcare facilities, allowing ICU placement above previous limits and enabling vertical expansion; could cut capacity-expansion costs by 20-25% and benefit listed hospital operators such as Apollo Hospitals Enterprises.
